topics.lesson_subject: Upstream TLS re-encryption for HTTP virtual load-balancing VIPs
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: HTTP server-load-balance VIP accepts client-side HTTP and independently initiates HTTPS/TLS to each selected real server; ssl-upstream is valid only with server-type http; response cookie and Location rewrite controls adapt HTTPS backend semantics to HTTP clients.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client TCP/HTTP request -> VIP selection/session -> FortiGate proxy terminates client leg -> TLS client handshake to realserver port -> HTTP request forwarded inside TLS -> response headers normalized -> client response.
topics.failure_class: Backend confidentiality gap or upstream TLS negotiation/certificate failure; response-header semantics break HTTP clients.
topics.evidence_pattern: Client curl receives HTTP status; backend-side packet capture shows TLS ClientHello/ServerHello and encrypted application records; realserver logs show request. HTTP 200 alone does not prove upstream encryption.
topics.remediation_path: Enable ssl-upstream on HTTP server-load-balance VIP; set realserver port to TLS listener; configure supported TLS versions and server certificate verification/trust; use client certificate only when backend requests mTLS; review Secure-cookie and Location conversion before enabling compatibility rewrites.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish front-end HTTP acceptance from independent backend TLS establishment and identify which packet evidence proves encryption on the realserver leg.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two-leg reverse-proxy topology: cleartext client-to-VIP segment, FortiGate VIP proxy boundary, TLS-encrypted VIP-to-realserver segment, response-header adaptation callout.

topics.lesson_subject: Central Firewall Users monitor: authentication-method and user-group filtering, VDOM identity, and session deauthentication
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0 Device Manager monitor presents currently logged-in firewall users organized by managed FortiGate, exposing authentication method, user-group membership, VDOM context, filters and a deauthenticate action.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Managed FortiGate maintains authenticated user/session state -> FortiManager Device Manager monitor presents per-device entries -> operator filters by method/group and VDOM -> deauthenticate action is issued to the selected user session.
topics.failure_class: Incorrectly scoped identity response or stale active session; operator confuses centralized visibility with policy-level denial.
topics.evidence_pattern: Monitor row plus Method, User Group and VDOM fields establish active identity context; successful deauthentication removes the current session but does not prove future authentication is blocked.
topics.remediation_path: Filter by both authentication method and group; use VDOM to disambiguate identical usernames; deauthenticate only the intended session; correct identity source/group membership or firewall policy if the user immediately reauthenticates.
topics.question_fingerprint: Separate session termination from durable authorization change and use VDOM plus authentication method to identify the correct user session.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager central monitor above three FortiGate/VDOM columns, user rows converging to a selected session and deauthentication control arrow.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiMQ connector for ADOM-scoped indicator block/unblock propagation to FortiGate
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Built-in FortiMQ connector sends FortiAnalyzer indicators to FortiGate external feeds without FortiManager; connector is ADOM-specific, requires same FortiCare account registration and FortiGate Cloud-based Fabric Feed synchronization; block_indicator playbook transports action.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate logs -> FortiAnalyzer ADOM -> operator creates/blocks IP, URL, domain or MAC indicator -> block_indicator playbook -> FortiMQ cloud -> same-ADOM FortiGate retrieves external-feed entry -> firewall policy/security profile consumes feed.
topics.failure_class: Threat indicator accepted in FortiAnalyzer but not delivered, synchronized to the wrong ADOM, or not enforced by a policy.
topics.evidence_pattern: Connector status proves cloud API connectivity; indicator presence in FortiGate external feed proves synchronization; matching deny-policy log proves enforcement. None alone proves the other stages.
topics.remediation_path: Verify both devices share FortiCare account, FortiGate logging and Cloud-based Fabric Feed sync are enabled, connector is active in the intended ADOM, feed is updated, and the relevant policy/profile references it. FortiMQ takes priority over FortiManager when both connectors are active.
topics.question_fingerprint: Trace the full indicator-to-enforcement chain and identify ADOM scope and connector priority rather than assuming a successful Block click equals policy enforcement.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer ADOM with indicator/playbook node, FortiMQ cloud relay, same-ADOM FortiGate external-feed object and firewall deny-policy terminal node.

topics.lesson_subject: sFlow v5 packet and counter sampling from FortiSwitch ports, trunks and VLANs to external collectors
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch sFlow v5 agent randomly samples packets and periodically exports interface counter samples as UDP sFlow datagrams to one or more collectors; supports ports, trunks and VLANs; sampling is statistical, not a full packet capture.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Collector configured in config system sflow -> per-interface packet sampler/rate/direction and counter interval configured -> switch samples ingress/egress frames and counters -> datagrams sent to collector (default UDP 6343) -> collector aggregates and visualizes flow/counter samples.
topics.failure_class: No exported samples, incorrect collector endpoint/port, sampler disabled on monitored interface, or collector data misinterpreted as full-fidelity capture.
topics.evidence_pattern: get system sflow shows agent/collector config; interface config shows sampler/rate; UDP capture on port 6343 proves datagrams leave switch; collector dashboard proves receipt. A ping proves IP reachability only, not sFlow export.
topics.remediation_path: Verify collector IP/UDP port, switch-to-collector reachability, firewall allowance, per-interface sampler enablement, sample rate and direction; inspect UDP 6343; verify sflowd process only if no packets are emitted; tune sample rate and polling interval for scale.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish sampled flow records from full packet capture and identify which stage is proven by collector reachability versus observed UDP datagrams.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple FortiSwitch ingress/egress ports feed an sFlow agent; separate packet-sample and counter-sample streams converge on UDP collector with a statistical-sampling annotation.

topics.lesson_subject: WIDS rogue-AP detection, radio scan duty cycle, accepted/rogue classification and MAC-adjacency tuning
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAP radios scan the operating band as dedicated monitors or briefly leave AP mode during background scans; WIDS profiles enable intrusion detectors and rogue-AP monitoring; detections are classified Accepted or Rogue and logged/uploaded to FortiAnalyzer.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: WIDS profile created -> attached to selected radio in FortiAP profile -> radio performs dedicated or background scan -> FortiGate correlates observed AP/BSSID/SSID and wired adjacency -> operator classifies Accepted/Rogue -> event log and optional FortiAnalyzer upload.
topics.failure_class: Rogue AP not observed because scan coverage/cadence is insufficient, or false rogue classification due to incomplete wired MAC adjacency; background scan disrupts active traffic.
topics.evidence_pattern: Rogue AP widget/table shows detected APs, SSID and vendor; logs show alert/warning; scan timestamps and channel coverage prove observation opportunity. Absence of a rogue record does not prove no AP exists outside scan coverage.
topics.remediation_path: Apply WIDS profile to correct radio, review scan channels and AP model radio capabilities, use dedicated monitor where continuous coverage is required, tune ap-bgscan-idle to reduce packet loss during busy periods, and adjust rogue-scan-mac-adjacency only with topology evidence.
topics.question_fingerprint: Explain why background scan can delay detection under load and why MAC adjacency changes classification rather than radio visibility.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAP dual-radio topology showing client-serving radio periodically switching to monitor mode, dedicated-monitor alternative, rogue AP beacon observation, wired MAC adjacency check and FortiAnalyzer log path.
topics.doc_type: FortiWiFi and FortiAP Configuration Guide + New Features/Release Guide

topics.lesson_subject: Rogue DHCP server detection using a dedicated interface, scheduled VLAN sweep and authorized-server/IP-helper inventory
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC uses a dedicated non-management interface and a System DHCP Port to move through explicitly configured VLANs on a schedule, observe DHCP servers and compare responders with the Authorized DHCP Servers group; IP-helper addresses require modeled IP/MAC entries.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Scheduled task selects VLAN -> System DHCP Port is brought down/up as VLAN membership changes -> DHCP discovery exchange occurs -> responding server identity compared with authorized group -> Rogue Host/Device DHCP Server event -> mapped alarm/notification.
topics.failure_class: Unauthorized DHCP responder not detected because VLAN omitted, scan interface/port incorrectly modeled, DHCP relay identity not authorized, or HA secondary cannot run scan.
topics.evidence_pattern: Task schedule/run status and selected VLAN list prove coverage; DHCP response source and MAC prove observed responder; event/alarm proves comparison outcome. No event does not prove VLAN is clean if it was not scanned.
topics.remediation_path: Use a dedicated interface with unused subnet; never use eth0 management; populate System DHCP Ports with the switch port carrying the scan interface; list every VLAN; add authorized servers and IP-helper pingable models with their MAC addresses; match interface/port settings on both HA nodes.
topics.question_fingerprint: Identify why an IP-helper relay address can be falsely classified as rogue and which topology inventory must be added to the Authorized DHCP Servers group.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC dedicated scan NIC -> switch System DHCP Port -> sequential VLAN access legs -> DHCP responders -> authorized server/IP-helper comparison -> event/alarm, with HA peer symmetry callout.

topics.lesson_subject: SNMPv3 trap ingestion for host/user add-modify-remove lifecycle and directory enrichment
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F accepts SNMPv3 traps from modeled pingable senders to add, modify or remove host/user database records using enterprise OIDs; MAC is required for host removal; existing LDAP directories enrich user records; global SNMP protocol selection affects all devices querying FortiNAC.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Trap sender sends SNMPv3 notification to FortiNAC management IP/port 161 -> engine/user/auth/privacy validation -> enterprise OID/action parsed -> host/user record created or updated/removed -> LDAP lookup enriches user -> Add/Modify/Remove Host/User event -> mapped alarm/action.
topics.failure_class: Trap dropped or ignored due to unmodeled sender, SNMPv3 credential/engine mismatch, global SNMP version incompatibility, disabled events or HA destination omission.
topics.evidence_pattern: Packet capture proves trap reaches port 161; decrypted SNMPv3 PDU proves OID and varbinds; Event Log Add/Modify/Remove Host/User proves processing; Host/User view proves resulting record. Trap arrival alone does not prove database mutation.
topics.remediation_path: Model sender as pingable on each receiving server, configure matching SNMPv3 credentials/security level, ensure all polling devices are compatible with the global SNMP version, send to primary and secondary management IPs in HA, enable relevant events and verify OID/action and MAC format.
topics.question_fingerprint: Trace SNMPv3 trap arrival through authentication, OID parsing, directory enrichment and host/user mutation; distinguish encrypted packet capture from confirmed record update.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: External switch/IPS trap sender -> SNMPv3 auth/privacy boundary -> FortiNAC-F trap parser -> LDAP enrichment -> host/user DB -> event/alarm, with HA dual-destination branch.

topics.lesson_subject: RADIUS EAP ECDH curve override for TLS handshake interoperability
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator RADIUS EAP uses an ordered ECDH_CURVE list during TLS-based EAP negotiation; FortiAuthenticator 8.0 adds a CLI override command; default curve preference is secp521r1:secp384r1:prime256v1.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Supplicant begins 802.1X/EAP -> NAS relays EAP in RADIUS -> FortiAuthenticator selects TLS/EAP method and ECDH curve from configured preference -> TLS handshake and certificate validation -> inner/client authentication -> Access-Accept/Reject.
topics.failure_class: TLS/EAP negotiation fails because peer implementations have incompatible supported elliptic curves or curve preference; admin misdiagnoses as user credential or CA failure.
topics.evidence_pattern: RADIUS/EAP debug identifies TLS handshake stage; client and server supported-curve lists establish compatibility; successful EAP-TLS proves mutual certificate/auth flow. A RADIUS Access-Reject alone does not identify curve negotiation as cause.
topics.remediation_path: Inventory supplicant/NAS supported curves and server certificate/key constraints; use diagnose authentication radius-eap-ecdh-curve to inspect/override the EAP curve preference using documented CLI syntax; preserve strongest mutually supported curves and retest one EAP method at a time.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish ECDH ephemeral key-exchange curve negotiation from certificate public-key curve validation and choose the correct EAP/RADIUS evidence.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Supplicant -> AP/switch NAS -> RADIUS EAP tunnel -> FortiAuthenticator TLS engine with ordered ECDH curve list -> certificate and inner-auth decision -> Access-Accept/Reject.

topics.lesson_subject: RADIUS Message-Authenticator response validation and compatibility control
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 adds Message-Authenticator attribute to RADIUS requests and a per-RADIUS-server require-message-authenticator option; enabled by default, it mandates validation of the Message-Authenticator in Access-Accept/Reject responses.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiPAM sends RADIUS Access-Request with Message-Authenticator -> RADIUS server validates request and produces response -> FortiPAM checks response Message-Authenticator when option enabled -> authentication result accepted/rejected -> privileged access workflow continues or fails.
topics.failure_class: RADIUS interoperability/authentication failure when server omits or incorrectly computes Message-Authenticator; unsafe workaround disables response validation.
topics.evidence_pattern: Packet capture confirms Attribute 80 in request and response; FortiPAM RADIUS test status and server debug identify validation failure; successful test does not prove every policy/user group grants access.
topics.remediation_path: Verify both sides support Message-Authenticator and share the correct secret; inspect packet Attribute 80 and HMAC calculation; keep validation enabled; disable only as a documented temporary exception for a server that cannot emit the attribute, then remediate server compatibility.
topics.question_fingerprint: Differentiate missing response Attribute 80 from a bad shared secret and identify the security trade-off of disabling mandatory response validation.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM RADIUS client request with Attribute 80 -> RADIUS server -> Access-Accept/Reject response with Attribute 80 -> FortiPAM validation gate -> PAM authentication outcome.

topics.lesson_subject: ClickHouse scheduled rule evaluation versus in-memory streaming and scheduled-via-SQL modes
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM rule evaluation offers Streaming, Scheduled and Scheduled via SQL modes; Scheduled and Scheduled via SQL require ClickHouse, use disk/SQL-oriented execution and support broader windows/complex analytics with different trigger-event, exception, clear-condition and testability limits.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Rule definition selects detection technology and evaluation mode -> streaming engine evaluates incoming events in memory or scheduled engine executes on configured time window/interval/time zone -> condition result creates incidents -> clear/exception logic controls lifecycle.
topics.failure_class: Rule misses or duplicates incidents because mode, query window, schedule, database type, trigger-event expectations or clear semantics are mismatched.
topics.evidence_pattern: Rule configuration proves selected evaluation mode; schedule/last execution and incident timestamps prove scheduled execution; trigger-event details are absent for Scheduled via SQL by design; streaming testability does not transfer to scheduled SQL.
topics.remediation_path: Choose Streaming for low-latency high-concurrency correlation; choose Scheduled for larger windows/complex analytics where disk I/O and scale trade-offs are acceptable; use Scheduled via SQL only on ClickHouse in Super/Global mode and design around its 100-incident cap, key-only exceptions, time-only clear and no trigger events.
topics.question_fingerprint: Select rule evaluation mode from latency, query-window, ClickHouse and trigger-event requirements; identify limitations unique to Scheduled via SQL.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Incoming event stream branches to in-memory streaming evaluator and ClickHouse scheduled SQL/disk scheduler; both converge on incident lifecycle with mode-specific evidence/limitations callouts.

topics.lesson_subject: Agent-based ZTNA destination ranges/CIDRs with port lists and port ranges
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE agent-based ZTNA private application objects can represent a single IP/FQDN or, with supported FortiClient, an IP range/CIDR and Any/single/list/range ports; the application is bound to a FortiGate ZTNA application gateway and referenced by endpoint-profile connection rules.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin defines gateway (FortiGate address/port) -> defines private application address/range and port set -> binds app to gateway -> endpoint profile references app -> FortiClient evaluates destination rule -> traffic reaches ZTNA reverse-proxy gateway and is authorized by identity/posture policy.
topics.failure_class: Destination is outside configured host/port match, unsupported FortiClient version hides range/port controls, or endpoint profile does not reference the application/gateway.
topics.evidence_pattern: Portal app object shows type/range/CIDR/ports and gateway; endpoint profile shows selected ZTNA application; FortiClient rule match and gateway logs prove connection. Object presence alone does not prove endpoint version compatibility or authorization.
topics.remediation_path: Use FortiClient for Windows 7.2.8 or later and set the FortiSASE instance default FortiClient version accordingly; configure precise IP range/CIDR and ports; bind correct gateway; reference application in endpoint profile; validate encryption and SAML browser settings separately.
topics.question_fingerprint: Explain why a broad subnet object with a port range is not active until the endpoint profile references it and the FortiClient version supports it.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSASE catalogue gateway and private-app range/port object -> endpoint profile rule -> FortiClient endpoint -> FortiGate ZTNA reverse proxy -> internal service.
topics.doc_type: Feature Administration Guide + Mature Administration Guide

topics.lesson_subject: Hybrid priority/SLA strategy: SLA value, cost, link-quality and configuration-order selection
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SLA-mode service rule can combine priority and SLA selection; members are ranked by highest SLA value, then administrative cost, then configured link-cost-factor quality, then cfg_order. Health-check custom-profile-1 can combine weighted packet loss, latency, jitter and reciprocal bidirectional bandwidth.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Health-check probes update member alive/SLA maps and metrics -> service rule filters eligible members -> SLA value ranking -> cost tie-break -> quality score tie-break -> cfg_order final tie-break -> route/SD-WAN selection and forwarding.
topics.failure_class: Unexpected member selection because operator assumes one metric controls selection, custom-profile weights/threshold are wrong, or link-cost-threshold/route regeneration is misunderstood.
topics.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys sdwan health-check proves liveness, SLA map and measured metrics; diagnose sys sdwan service4 proves candidate ordering and selected member; packet capture on chosen interface proves actual forwarding. Probe pass alone does not prove service-rule winner.
topics.remediation_path: Validate health-check weights and thresholds, `set tie-break priority`, selected `link-cost-factor`, `custom-profile-threshold`, member costs and cfg_order; inspect service4 after metric changes; set link-cost-threshold deliberately to avoid excessive route regeneration.
topics.question_fingerprint: Apply the four-level hybrid ranking order to members with different SLA values, costs, quality metrics and cfg_order; distinguish SLA eligibility from quality ranking.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Health-check measurement plane feeds SLA bitmaps and custom quality score; service-rule decision diamond ranks SLA value, cost, link quality and cfg_order before selected WAN member.
